text:
maria.k: FYI seeing intermittent connection drops from the rack-5 internal L4 -> gpushare pool. Affects a subset of GPU pods (OOM/restart-ish), started ~2026-03-17T10:12:00Z. Roughly 1-3% new TCP handshakes failing, skewed to one ToR pair.

ajay.r: Can you share the LB metrics/err counts and any tcpdump/sniff?

maria.k: infra-bot posted alert earlier: 
infra-bot: [ALERT] top-rack-lb: SYN retries > 1% (10m) in rack-5 -> triggering page.

maria.k: quick metric snapshot: p50 conn latency 2ms, p95 6ms, p99 120ms; SYN retry rate 1.8% over last 5m. Backend success ratio for gpushare pool ~98.9%.

samir: I checked conntrack on a few affected K8s nodes, counts are high and entries for client->gpushare are timing out. see: 
```
$ sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
420123
$ sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
524288
```
seems high but below limit. However many entries are in ESTABLISHED->CLOSE_WAIT weirdly.

ajay.r: can you tcpdump a syn/handshake on the ToR-facing interface and from a pod side? also include tcp resets.

maria.k: pasted short tcpdump extract (trimmed):
```
10:12:08.123456 IP pod-abc.34212 > tor5:9100: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0], length 0
10:12:08.123457 IP tor5:9100 > pod-abc.34212: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 29200, options [mss 9000], length 0
10:12:08.123458 IP pod-abc.34212 > tor5:9100: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0
```
notice the ToR replies with S but next packet from pod is R sometimes.

oncall-tej: Could be asymmetric forwarding or sticky-hash mismatch if ToR uses 5-tuple hashing vs our LB pseudo. Any recent ToR firmware or config changes?

maria.k: No recent infra change on our side. netops-liz, any config pushed to tor5 this morning?

netops-liz: We rolled a minor ASIC microcode patch on tor5 at 09:50 for bgp NHT bug, vendor said no data-plane impact but will re-check. Also seeing ECN/MTU mismatch logs on tor5 after the patch.

samir: MTU mismatch could explain the R if kernel rejects path. I ran `ip -s link show dev eth0` on a node and saw tx errors on the host-facing interface around the same window. Also RDMA not in use on these nodes but jumbo frames are enabled.

maria.k: Action plan suggestion: 1) cordon/gently drain a couple of affected k8s nodes from rack-5 gpushare service, schedule them to different racks; 2) netops to rollback microcode on tor5 or put it in maintenance; 3) capture full packet trace (pod->ToR->backend) and conntrack dump; 4) increase conntrack timeout for ephemeral entries temporarily.

ajay.r: +1. We should move hot GPU jobs first (priority queues) to avoid failed runs and cost/credits churn. I'll create a quick k8s evacuation job for top 10 pods by mem.

netops-liz: starting rollback now on tor5 and will put it in degraded maintenance mode so traffic shifts. Will post timing.

infra-bot: [INFO] rollback job queued for tor5 microcode at 10:24 UTC.

samir: I dumped conntrack entries around the spike, saved to /tmp/ct-dump-rack5.log — pattern: repeated half-open entries then immediate R from host side. Also noticed a bunch of entries with L4 hash mismatch across two ToRs for same src/dst.

maria.k: moving two workers now (drain) — jobs rescheduled to rack-2 and rack-9. Observed immediate drop in SYN retries to ~0.2% for moved traffic within 30s. Seems correlated.

netops-liz: rollback finished at 10:28 UTC, tor5 in maintenance. Vendor confirmed the microcode produced an unexpected flow-path for TCP syn with large MSS -> causing mismatched ECN/MTU handling. They've opened a ticket for a new build.

maria.k: post-rollback metrics: SYN retry rate down to 0.25%, p99 conn latency back to 9-15ms. GPU job failures stopped.

ajay.r: good catch. followups: (a) make a runbook for ToR microcode rollbacks + quick k8s evacuation steps; (b) disable jumbo frames on gpushare pool hosts until vendor fix is validated; (c) add conntrack counts and SYN-retry alert to the gpushare SLO dashboard.

maria.k: I'll draft the runbook and add the alert. tagging @netops-liz and @oncall-tej to coordinate vendor support and verify the fix in staging before re-enabling jumbo. :thumbsup:

netops-liz: will coordinate with vendor and post updates in this thread. Thanks everyone.
